episode.title: Fail closed when tool-call completion evidence is ambiguous, reused, or truncated
episode.before: At parent b348fc26674189f758d5941cdab3f78f258b2aa7, the recorder began without indexing initial-history identifiers, treated every registered runtime cell as newly started, did not reject duplicate nested call IDs, and did not verify that recorded exec/wait outputs had a unique matching input. Prompt budgeting could revoke completion broadly when evidence was truncated, and recorder allocation was fixed at session construction rather than following eligible runtime configuration refreshes.
episode.after: At 03f014564deef528c25e80fe67ec51871cb6ee51, the recorder indexes bounded call-ID evidence from initial history, tracks call and runtime-cell reuse, and marks completion incomplete whenever freshness cannot be proved. Prompt attachment verifies unique input/output associations, propagates irreversible invalidation across outputs belonging to an affected runtime cell, and withholds wait completion after resume or fork. Metadata budgeting replaces an over-budget output's inventory with a local omission marker and clears completion only for outputs sharing the damaged cell. Recording enablement can be refreshed independently from execution features while legacy reloads preserve the live recorder.
episode.diff: The change modifies 12 files with 1,772 insertions and 638 deletions. It adds a bounded monotonic SeenIds filter; passes InitialHistory into recorder construction; adds origin, runtime-cell, duplicate-call, and exec/wait association checks; makes retained completeness fail closed across retries and compaction; rewrites request-budget handling around per-output omission markers and cell-scoped completion invalidation; adds runtime recorder refresh handling; and adds unit and integration regressions for reused IDs, missing or paginated history, mismatched wrappers, resumed waits, compaction, unrelated truncation, and runtime enablement.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit identifies reused call IDs, ambiguous exec/wait associations, missing history, and cross-cell truncation effects as causes of unreliable completeness claims, and states that the resolution tracks IDs, validates associations, localizes truncation, and refreshes recording enablement.
The parent recorder constructor accepted only feature state, allocated optional immutable recorder storage, did not index history, and unconditionally changed a registered cell to Started.

SeenIds uses a bounded monotonic bitmap with separate call-ID and runtime-cell namespaces, indexes identifiers from normal and compacted initial history subject to entry and byte limits, and reports history_ids_indexed=false when complete indexing cannot be established.

Recorder initialization now consumes InitialHistory, permits wait-completion proof only for new or cleared history, and starts a cell only when its runtime ID and origin are fresh and history identifiers were successfully indexed; otherwise it makes the cell incomplete.

Repeated wrapper origins, direct call IDs, runtime-cell IDs, and nested call IDs invalidate completion; invalidation is propagated to retained records associated with the affected origin or runtime cell.

Prompt attachment counts outputs, records only unique input positions, validates that each exec or wait input precedes and semantically matches its output, rejects direct-call collisions, and prevents a retained incomplete record from becoming complete again after inventory or association evidence is lost.

Prompt attachment withholds completion for ordinary wait outputs when the session came from resumed or forked history because runtime cell handles may be reused, while direct exec output can still be certified from locally observed evidence.

Protocol budgeting now tracks damaged cell identifiers, clears completeness across only those cells, sheds optional result metadata and sources before call evidence, and replaces an over-budget output's own calls with a local omission marker rather than using a global omission fallback.
Session construction passes initial history to the recorder, making historical call identifiers part of the completion-proof boundary.

Normal runtime configuration refresh updates recorder enablement independently of execution features, while legacy configuration reload explicitly skips recorder refresh to preserve the current live recorder.

Recorder-level regressions cover lossless completion, paginated history, forked waits, wrapper mismatch, reused origins, direct-ID collision, truncation after compaction, missing historical evidence, and preservation of unrelated complete outputs under overflow.

End-to-end Code Mode regressions exercise ID knowledge after compaction, runtime recording enablement, recorder preservation across refresh, resumed wait cell reuse, and survival of an unrelated complete call during truncation.

Protocol tests assert that completeness is host-only and fail-closed, raw result metadata is shed before stronger evidence, and metadata budgeting retains evidence without allowing one damaged cell to certify another output.

The implementation supplies layered regression oracles at bounded-ID unit, recorder/request-metadata, protocol-budgeting, and end-to-end Code Mode levels; the evidence bundle does not report an executed test command or status-check result.

candidate_atomics.name: index_observed_identifiers_for_freshness
candidate_atomics.title: Index observed identifiers before certifying freshness
candidate_atomics.description: Maintain bounded, monotonic knowledge of historical and live identifiers so reused or unindexable identifiers cannot be treated as fresh evidence for completion.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent identifier reuse or unavailable history from producing a false tool-call completion claim.
semantic_action.pre_state: A recorder may encounter call origins or runtime handles that were already present in initial history, reused during the session, or unavailable because historical indexing exceeded a safety bound.
semantic_action.post_state: Completion can begin only for identifiers proven fresh against bounded historical and live observations; collisions, oversized identifiers, and incomplete history indexing fail closed.
semantic_action.validation: Bounded-filter tests verify namespace separation and saturation behavior; recorder tests verify that paginated known IDs and reused origins are rejected while genuinely fresh origins remain usable.

candidate_atomics.name: validate_tool_input_output_associations
candidate_atomics.title: Validate tool input and output associations
candidate_atomics.description: Verify that every completion-bearing output has one preceding, type-correct exec or wait input with the expected origin and runtime handle, and make any loss of that evidence irreversible for the affected cell.

semantic_action.intent: Withhold completeness when wrappers, outputs, retries, or resumed runtime handles are ambiguous or inconsistent.
semantic_action.pre_state: Recorded calls may be attached to duplicated outputs, mismatched wrappers, reused origins, colliding direct calls, resumed waits, or retry history whose association evidence has changed.
semantic_action.post_state: Only a unique, ordered, type-correct association can retain completeness, and once the associated inventory or mapping is invalidated all retained outputs for that runtime cell remain incomplete.
semantic_action.validation: Recorder regressions cover mismatched wrappers, reused origins, duplicate IDs, forked waits, and retry/compaction loss; end-to-end tests cover resumed runtime-cell reuse and compaction.

candidate_atomics.name: localize_metadata_budget_damage
candidate_atomics.title: Localize metadata-budget damage to affected cells
candidate_atomics.description: Apply request-size limits per output, preserve stronger evidence before optional metadata, and revoke completion only where truncation or omission damaged the recorded inventory.

semantic_action.intent: Keep unrelated complete tool-call inventories trustworthy when another output exceeds the metadata budget.
semantic_action.pre_state: Serialized tool-call metadata exceeds argument, per-output, or request limits, so some evidence must be truncated or omitted.
semantic_action.post_state: Optional result metadata and sources are shed first; an over-budget output carries its own omission marker; completion is cleared for every output sharing the damaged cell but remains available to intact unrelated cells.
semantic_action.validation: Protocol tests exercise budget priority and fail-closed completion, recorder tests preserve an unrelated complete exec under overflow, and an end-to-end Code Mode test verifies the same behavior.

candidate_atomics.name: refresh_recording_state_without_execution_drift
candidate_atomics.title: Refresh recording state without changing execution behavior
candidate_atomics.description: Allow runtime rollout configuration to enable or disable evidence recording independently from tool dispatch, while preventing stale legacy snapshots from replacing a valid live recorder.

semantic_action.intent: Keep metadata recording aligned with current runtime policy without altering which tools can execute or falsely certifying calls made before recording began.
semantic_action.pre_state: A session's recording rollout may change after construction, or a legacy reload may carry the session's original feature snapshot rather than current host policy.
semantic_action.post_state: Normal runtime refresh atomically creates or removes recorder state without changing execution gates; late-created state marks prior history unobserved, and legacy reload preserves the existing recorder.
semantic_action.validation: Recorder and end-to-end tests verify runtime enablement, absence of completeness when earlier history was unobserved, and preservation of prepared call bindings across refresh.

candidate_workflows.name: harden_structured_tool_completion_proofs
candidate_workflows.title: Harden structured tool-call completion proofs
candidate_workflows.description: A fail-closed resolution chain for completion metadata that crosses session history, asynchronous exec/wait wrappers, retries, compaction, and bounded prompt serialization.

workflow_graph.goal: Emit a positive structured completion claim only when the host retains an unambiguous, lossless chain from a fresh invocation through its nested calls and matching output, while preserving valid claims for unrelated cells.
when_to_use: A host records nested tool activity and exposes a structured completeness marker to a later model request or downstream consumer.
Invocation or runtime identifiers can be reused across retries, compaction, resume, fork, or asynchronous wait operations.
Recorded evidence is subject to per-call or aggregate serialization budgets.
Recording policy can change during a long-lived session.
anti_goals: Do not change tool execution availability, dispatch gates, or nested-tool behavior merely to change recording policy.
Do not infer completeness from a successful wrapper callback, terminal wait, or retained marker when association or inventory evidence is missing.
Do not discard trustworthy metadata for unrelated cells solely because one cell exceeded a budget.
Do not use unbounded sets or unbounded hashing to prove identifier freshness.
not_applicable_when: The metadata is informational only and no consumer interprets it as a complete inventory or proof.
Invocation identifiers and output associations are guaranteed unique and immutable by a stronger external protocol, with no retries, resume, fork, compaction, or truncation boundary.
No host-side execution evidence can be inspected; in that case a positive completion contract cannot be established.
inputs: Initial session history, including compacted replacement history when available
Live tool input and output items with call identifiers and tool type information
Runtime cell identifiers and originating wrapper identifiers
Recorded nested-call inventory and retained retry state
Per-argument, per-output, and aggregate metadata budgets
Current and incoming runtime recording feature state
workflow_graph.entry_state: The system can record nested calls, but identifier freshness, wrapper association, retry integrity, budget truncation, or runtime enablement may allow an unsupported completeness marker.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every positive completion marker is backed by fresh identifiers, a unique matching input/output association, and an intact recorded inventory within the serialized prompt; ambiguous or damaged cells are incomplete, unrelated intact cells remain complete, and recording policy changes do not alter execution behavior.

steps.condition: Always required when identifiers can cross history or recorder-lifetime boundaries.
steps.validation: Known historical and repeated identifiers return non-fresh; failed indexing prevents cell start from becoming completion-eligible.

steps.condition: Apply when attaching recorded evidence to outputs or replaying retained evidence after retry or compaction.
steps.validation: Each certified output has exactly one preceding type-correct exec or wait input, matching origin/runtime handle, no direct-call collision, and an intact retained inventory.

steps.condition: Apply before sending or storing metadata whenever argument or aggregate limits can truncate recorded evidence.
steps.validation: Damaged cells lose completion across their outputs, their omission marker remains local, and unrelated intact cells retain completion under the global budget.

steps.condition: Apply when recorder enablement is controlled by runtime rollout or configuration refresh.
steps.validation: Runtime enablement changes recorder allocation without changing execution features; late enablement cannot certify unobserved history; legacy reload keeps the live recorder.

validation_ladder: Unit-test bounded identifier tracking, namespace separation, saturation, historical indexing limits, and repeated-ID rejection.
Test recorder state transitions for lossless completion, duplicate nested IDs, wrapper mismatches, direct-call collisions, forked or resumed waits, retries, and compaction.
Test protocol serialization budgets to confirm optional metadata is shed before core evidence and completion is revoked only for damaged cells.
Run end-to-end asynchronous tool scenarios for runtime enablement, configuration refresh, resumed handle reuse, compaction, and unrelated-output truncation.
stop_conditions: Stop and withhold completeness if initial-history identifiers cannot be indexed within bounds and freshness is required.
Stop and invalidate the affected cell if an origin, runtime handle, or nested call ID is reused or collides.
Stop and invalidate retained completion if an output is duplicated, lacks one matching preceding input, changes inventory, or no longer matches its exec/wait wrapper.
Stop and clear completion for the affected cell when truncation or omission prevents retention of its full call inventory.
Stop extraction-level validation short of claiming a green build because the evidence bundle contains test sources but no executed status-check or test-command result.
unresolved_or_deferred: The GitHub bundle lacks PR discussion, reviews, and status-check results.
No test command was executed as part of this extraction, so repository-wide runtime validation remains unconfirmed.
The bounded bitmap intentionally permits false-positive collisions that withhold completion; its production collision rate is not established by this episode.

unresolved_questions: Were the cited unit and integration suites executed successfully for the pinned commit? The available bundle contains test code and the commit's testing description but no status-check results.
What production frequency of bounded-filter collisions or history-index limit exhaustion is observed? The implementation deliberately fails closed in either case.
